title: Workspace Monitoring — configure collection and query diagnostics
summary: Workspace Monitoring provisions a read-only monitoring Eventhouse/KQL database that collects diagnostic logs and metrics from Fabric items. The preview Monitoring REST API is exposed through 'fabio monitoring' for item CRUD, definitions, and data-collection enable/disable; query the destination data with 'fabio kql-database query'.
api_surface: Use 'fabio monitoring create/update/delete/get-definition/update-definition' to manage the Monitoring item and 'enable-data-collection'/'disable-data-collection' to control collection. The API is preview. Per-workload settings that are absent from MonitoringProperties.json, such as an eventstream's 'Log Eventstream activity' toggle, may still require that workload's portal or API surface.

enablement.tenant_setting: The tenant setting 'Workspace admins can turn on monitoring for their workspaces' (settingName: PlatformMonitoringTenantSetting) must be ON. fabio CAN set it (admin): fabio admin update-tenant-setting --setting-name PlatformMonitoringTenantSetting --content '{"enabled": true}'
enablement.per_workspace: Create a Monitoring item with 'fabio monitoring create --workspace $WS --name Monitoring_1 --file MonitoringProperties.json', then enable collection with 'fabio monitoring enable-data-collection --workspace $WS --id $MONITORING'. The caller needs write permission on the item and workspace Admin to enable or disable collection.
enablement.per_eventstream_toggle: Eventstream observability is OFF by default per eventstream. Enable 'Log Eventstream activity' in each eventstream's Settings panel (portal-only) — a workspace with 10 eventstreams can monitor just the 2-3 critical ones.
prerequisites: Power BI Premium or Fabric capacity
Log Analytics NOT enabled in the same workspace (mutually exclusive)

query_the_data_with_fabio.note: The destination monitoring Eventhouse is a normal KQL database item in the workspace. Manage collection with 'fabio monitoring'; query the collected records with the existing KQL commands.
query_the_data_with_fabio.find_it: fabio kql-database list --workspace $WS   # locate the monitoring KQL database (auto-created by enablement)
query_the_data_with_fabio.query: fabio kql-database query --workspace $WS --id $MON_KQLDB --kql "EventStreamErrorMetrics | where Timestamp > ago(1h) | summarize count() by ErrorCode, Severity"
query_the_data_with_fabio.schema: fabio kql-database query --workspace $WS --id $MON_KQLDB --kql ".show tables"   # list the available monitoring tables (then '<Table> | getschema' for columns)

other_workloads: Data Factory: Pipeline activity run logs; Copy job activity run details
Data Engineering: GraphQL metrics + operation logs
Power BI: Semantic model operation logs

constraints: Only one Monitoring item per workspace can collect data at a time. Enabling another returns WSMDataCollectionAlreadyEnabledInWorkspace; disable the current item first.
Enable and disable are idempotent and leave MonitoringProperties.json unchanged.
A Monitoring definition uses format MonitoringV1 and the MonitoringProperties.json part. dataCollectionSettings, when present, must contain exactly one complete source/destination mapping.
After configuration, Eventhouse mode and a linked parent Monitoring reference cannot be changed or removed. An enabled operationsAgent cannot be disabled or removed.
The destination monitoring Eventhouse is read-only from its data plane; manage collection and its definition through the Monitoring item.
Retention is 30 days; ingestion CANNOT be filtered by log type/category (e.g. only errors).
Workspace monitoring and Log Analytics are mutually exclusive per workspace.
Monitoring Eventhouse/Eventstream operations are not throttled by capacity state, but Power BI reports/Activator alerts built on the monitoring DB ARE throttled.
If a table is missing, toggle 'Log workspace activity' off then on in the Monitoring tab (the Eventhouse predates that table).
